analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It adds the DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES row to the launchd passthrough table in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1751). It also changes the documented DARKBLOOM_PREFILL_DEADLINE_MODE default in docs/reference/configuration.md (lines 413-414) from off, which enabled enforcement only on 'enforce', to enforce unless the value is exactly 'off'. The configuration.md patch excerpt is truncated, and no head text for that file was supplied. I could not check the rest of that change or the source behind it.

No code, authentication, attestation, encryption, or trust-boundary change is visible. The passthrough table row is a documentation entry. The docs say the variable is read by AdmissionRateEstimators.swift and forwarded to the LaunchAgent plist. It tunes TTFT admission and prefill deadlines, which relate to availability under T-010 and T-029. Nothing in the supplied text affects A-001 prompt confidentiality, A-003 keys, A-016 serving authorization, or the T-041 prefix-cache posture.

The prefill-deadline default flip to enforce is a documented behaviour change. If the source does flip it, requests exceeding the deadline could be rejected, which is an availability and performance matter. Whether the documentation matches the source change is unverified here. This is not evidence of a security regression. A next pass should confirm that PrefillDeadlineMode.resolve and AdmissionRateEstimators.swift match the docs, and that the passthrough list in LaunchAgent.swift includes the new key. Passthrough of an operator-set tuning env var from the invoking user's shell is consistent with the existing pattern and crosses no new boundary. No findings.
